99	class Engine:
100	    """A small relational store persisted in one directory."""
101	
102	    def __init__(self, root, now_ms=None, page_size=PAGE_SIZE):
103	        self.root = os.path.abspath(root)
104	        self.page_size = int(page_size)
105	        self._now_ms = now_ms
106	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
107	        self.pager = Pager(self.root, self.page_size)
108	        self._reset()
109	        self._load()
110	
111	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ basics
112	    def _now(self):
113	        source = self._now_ms
114	        if source is None:
115	            return int(time.time() * 1000)
116	        return int(source() if callable(source) else source)
117	
118	    def _reset(self):
119	        self.tables = {}
120	        self._indexes = {}
121	        self._audit = []
122	        self._committed = set()
123	        self._open = set()
124	        self._horizon = 0
125	        self._base_horizon = 0
126	        self._next_txid = 1
127	        self._commit_counter = 0
128	        self._commit_seq = {}
129	        self.lsn = 0
130	
131	    def _is_committed(self, txid):
132	        return txid in self._committed or txid <= self._base_horizon
133	
134	    def _table(self, name):
135	        table = self.tables.get(name)
136	        if table is None:
137	            raise StorageError("unknown table %s" % name)
138	        return table
139	
140	    def has_table(self, name):
141	        return name in self.tables
142	
143	    def list_tables(self):
144	        with self._lock:
145	            return sorted(self.tables)
146	
147	    def table_info(self, name):
148	        with self._lock:
149	            table = self._table(name)
150	            return {
151	                "name": name,
152	                "columns": [self._column_info(col) for col in table["columns"]],
153	                "primary_key": table["primary_key"],
154	                "indexes": dict(table["indexes"]),
155	                "rows": len(table["rows"]),
156	            }
157	
158	    @staticmethod
159	    def _column_info(column):
160	        info = dict(column)
161	        if info.get("references") is not None:
162	            info["references"] = dict(info["references"])
163	        return info
164	
165	    def _reader(self):
166	        """Pseudo transaction used for engine level reads (txid 0 writes nothing)."""
167	        return Transaction(self, 0, self._horizon)
168	
169	    def _coerce_pk(self, table, pk):
170	        column = [c for c in table["columns"] if c["name"] == table["primary_key"]][0]
171	        if isinstance(pk, str):
172	            if column["type"] == "int":
173	                try:
174	                    return int(pk)
175	                except ValueError:
176	                    raise StorageError("primary key %r is not an int" % pk)
177	            if column["type"] == "bool":
178	                if pk.lower() in ("true", "1"):
179	                    return True
180	                if pk.lower() in ("false", "0"):
181	                    return False
182	                raise StorageError("primary key %r is not a bool" % pk)
183	        return pk
184	
185	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- MVCC
186	    def _visible(self, versions, txid, horizon):
187	        """Newest version of a row visible to ``txid`` at ``horizon``."""
188	        best = None
189	        for version in versions:
190	            created = version["created"]
191	            deleted = version["deleted"]
192	            if created != txid and not (self._is_committed(created) and created <= horizon):
193	                continue
194	            if deleted is None or deleted == txid:
195	                best = version
196	            elif not (self._is_committed(deleted) and deleted <= horizon):
197	                best = version
198	        return best
199	
200	    def _conflicting_writes(self, versions, tx):
201	        """First version written by another transaction after ``tx`` started."""
202	        for version in versions:
203	            for marker in (version["created"], version["deleted"]):
204	                if marker is None or marker == tx.txid:
205	                    continue
206	                if marker > tx.snapshot or not self._is_committed(marker):
207	                    return version
208	        return None
209	
210	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- read paths
211	    def _record_read(self, tx, entry):
212	        """Remember a read predicate of a serializable transaction.
213	
214	        Entries are ``("pk", table, pk)``, ``("range", table, column, low,
215	        high)`` or ``("where", table, conds)`` with an empty ``conds`` meaning
216	        the whole table.  Only successful reads are recorded, and only when
217	        the caller is not suppressing recording (see ``Transaction.query``).
218	        """
219	        if tx.isolation == "serializable" and not tx._suppress:
220	            tx._reads.append(entry)
221	
222	    def _scan(self, tx, table):
223	        table_obj = self._table(table)
224	        rows = []
225	        for pk in sorted(table_obj["rows"], key=query.sort_key):
226	            version = self._visible(table_obj["rows"][pk], tx.txid, tx.snapshot)
227	            if version is not None:
228	                rows.append(dict(version["values"]))
229	        self._record_read(tx, ("where", table, ()))
230	        return rows
231	
232	    def _get(self, tx, table, pk):
233	        table_obj = self._table(table)
234	        pk = self._coerce_pk(table_obj, pk)
235	        versions = table_obj["rows"].get(pk)
236	        version = self._visible(versions, tx.txid, tx.snapshot) if versions else None
237	        self._record_read(tx, ("pk", table, pk))
238	        return dict(version["values"]) if version is not None else None
239	
240	    def _index_lookup(self, tx, table, column, low, high):
241	        """Rows whose current version falls inside [low, high], in index order.
242	
243	        Stale entries left behind by superseded versions are filtered out by
244	        checking the value of the version this transaction can actually see.
245	        """
246	        table_obj = self._table(table)
247	        if column not in table_obj["indexes"]:
248	            raise StorageError("no index on %s.%s" % (table, column))
249	        tree = self._indexes.get((table, column))
250	        rows = []
251	        seen = set()
252	        for value, pk in (tree.iter_range(low, high) if tree is not None else ()):
253	            if pk in seen:
254	                continue
255	            versions = table_obj["rows"].get(pk)
256	            version = self._visible(versions, tx.txid, tx.snapshot) if versions else None
257	            if version is None:
258	                continue
259	            current = version["values"].get(column)
260	            if current is None or current != value:
261	                continue  # stale entry of a superseded version
262	            if (low is not None and current < low) or (high is not None and current > high):
263	                continue
264	            seen.add(pk)
265	            rows.append(dict(version["values"]))
266	        self._record_read(tx, ("range", table, column, low, high))
267	        return rows
268	
269	    # -------------------------------------------------- serializable checking
270	    def _predicate_matches(self, entry, values):
271	        """True when a written row image falls inside a protected read range."""
272	        if entry[0] == "where":
273	            return all(query.compare(op, values.get(col), val) for col, op, val in entry[2])
274	        _, _, column, low, high = entry
275	        value = values.get(column)
276	        if value is None:
277	            return False  # null values are never part of an index range
278	        try:
279	            if low is not None and value < low:
280	                return False
281	            if high is not None and value > high:
282	                return False
283	        except TypeError:
284	            return False
285	        return True
286	
287	    def _check_read_conflicts(self, tx):
288	        """Validate a serializable transaction against newer committed writes.
289	
290	        Every version written by a transaction that committed after ``tx``
291	        started — whatever its isolation level or start order — is checked
292	        against the predicates ``tx`` recorded while reading.  A write to a
293	        protected primary key, or a written row whose image before or after
294	        the write matches a protected predicate, is a read-write conflict.
295	        """
296	        by_table = {}
297	        for entry in tx._reads:
298	            by_table.setdefault(entry[1], []).append(entry)
299	        for table, entries in by_table.items():
300	            table_obj = self.tables.get(table)
301	            if table_obj is None:
302	                continue
303	            protected_pks = {entry[2] for entry in entries if entry[0] == "pk"}
304	            matchers = [entry for entry in entries if entry[0] != "pk"]
305	            for pk, versions in table_obj["rows"].items():
306	                for version in versions:
307	                    newer = False
308	                    for marker in (version["created"], version["deleted"]):
309	                        if marker is None or marker == tx.txid:
310	                            continue
311	                        if self._commit_seq.get(marker, 0) > tx._commit_horizon:
312	                            newer = True
313	                            break
314	                    if not newer:
315	                        continue
316	                    if pk in protected_pks:
317	                        raise ConflictError(
318	                            "key %r of table %s was written by a transaction "
319	                            "that committed after transaction %d started" % (pk, table, tx.txid)
320	                        )
321	                    if any(self._predicate_matches(m, version["values"]) for m in matchers):
322	                        raise ConflictError(
323	                            "a transaction that committed after transaction %d started "
324	                            "wrote rows matching its reads on table %s" % (tx.txid, table)
325	                        )
326	
327	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ write paths
328	    def _read_json(self, page_id):
329	        payload = self.pager.read_page(page_id).rstrip(b"\x00")
330	        if not payload:
331	            raise StorageError("page %d is empty" % page_id)
332	        return json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"))
333	
334	    def _read_pages(self, first_page, count, length):
335	        chunks = [self.pager.read_page(first_page + i) for i in range(int(count))]
336	        return b"".join(chunks)[: int(length)]
337	
338	    def _load(self):
339	        if self.pager.page_count() == 0:
340	            return
341	        meta = self._read_json(META_PAGE)
342	        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or meta.get("format") != STATE_FORMAT:
343	            raise StorageError("page 0 does not hold a %s meta record" % STATE_FORMAT)
344	        self.lsn = int(meta.get("lsn", 0))
345	        self._horizon = int(meta.get("horizon", 0))
346	        self._base_horizon = self._horizon
347	        self._next_txid = max(int(meta.get("next_txid", 1)), self._horizon + 1)
348	        blob = self._read_pages(meta["state_page"], meta["state_pages"], meta["state_len"])
349	        state = json.loads(blob.decode("utf-8"))
350	        if state.get("format") != DB_FORMAT:
351	            raise StorageError("state blob has an unknown format")
352	        for name, info in state.get("tables", {}).items():
353	            table = {
354	                "name": name,
355	                "columns": info["columns"],
356	                "primary_key": info["primary_key"],
357	                "indexes": {col: "%s_%s_idx" % (name, col) for col in info.get("indexes", [])},
358	                "rows": {},
359	            }
360	            for pk, values in info["rows"]:
361	                table["rows"][pk] = [{"created": self._horizon, "deleted": None, "values": values}]
362	            self.tables[name] = table
363	            self._rebuild_indexes(table)
364	        index_refs = state.get("index_refs")
365	        if index_refs is not None:
366	            # A current image carries paged B+ tree indexes; they must load
367	            # cleanly and match the committed row state, otherwise the image
368	            # is refused instead of silently serving wrong index results.
369	            # Older images have no index pages and keep the in-memory indexes
370	            # rebuilt above, which yields the same query results.
371	            self._check_index_pages(index_refs)
372	        audit_blob = self._read_pages(meta["audit_page"], meta["audit_pages"], meta["audit_len"])
373	        self._audit = json.loads(audit_blob.decode("utf-8")) if audit_blob else []
374	        self._validate_foreign_keys()
375	
376	    def _validate_foreign_keys(self):
377	        """Reject loaded state whose foreign keys do not hold.
378	
379	        Every ``references`` entry must name an existing table's primary key
380	        of the same type, and every non-null foreign key value in a visible
381	        row must resolve to a visible parent row.  Anything else means the
382	        state on disk is not one this engine could have committed, so it is
383	        refused with :class:`StorageError`.
384	        """
385	        for name, table in self.tables.items():
386	            for column in table["columns"]:
387	                ref = column.get("references")
388	                if ref is None:
389	                    continue
390	                if not isinstance(ref, dict) or set(ref) != {"table", "column"}:
391	                    raise StorageError(
392	                        "table %s column %s has a malformed references entry"
393	                        % (name, column["name"])
394	                    )
395	                parent = self.tables.get(ref["table"])
396	                if parent is None:
397	                    raise StorageError(
398	                        "table %s column %s references unknown table %s"
399	                        % (name, column["name"], ref["table"])
400	                    )
401	                if ref["column"] != parent["primary_key"]:
402	                    raise StorageError(
403	                        "table %s column %s references %s.%s, which is not the primary key"
404	                        % (name, column["name"], ref["table"], ref["column"])
405	                    )
406	                pk_column = [c for c in parent["columns"] if c["name"] == parent["primary_key"]][0]
407	                if pk_column["type"] != column["type"]:
408	                    raise StorageError(
409	                        "table %s column %s has type %s but references %s.%s of type %s"
410	                        % (name, column["name"], column["type"],
411	                           ref["table"], ref["column"], pk_column["type"])
412	                    )
413	        for name, table in self.tables.items():
414	            fk_columns = [c for c in table["columns"] if c.get("references") is not None]
415	            if not fk_columns:
416	                continue
417	            for pk, versions in table["rows"].items():
418	                version = self._visible(versions, None, self._horizon)
419	                if version is None:
420	                    continue
421	                for column in fk_columns:
422	                    value = version["values"].get(column["name"])
423	                    if value is None:
424	                        continue
425	                    parent = self.tables[column["references"]["table"]]
426	                    parent_versions = parent["rows"].get(value)
427	                    found = self._visible(parent_versions, None, self._horizon) if parent_versions else None
428	                    if found is None:
429	                        raise StorageError(
430	                            "table %s row %r has a dangling reference: no row %r in table %s"
431	                            % (name, pk, value, column["references"]["table"])
432	                        )
433	
434	    def _write_chunks(self, txid, first_page, blob):
435	        size = self.pager.payload_size
436	        count = max(1, -(-len(blob) // size))
437	        for index in range(count):
438	            self.pager.write_page(txid, first_page + index, blob[index * size:(index + 1) * size])
439	        return count
440	
441	    def _snapshot(self):
442	        tables = {}
443	        for name, table in self.tables.items():
444	            rows = []
445	            for pk in sorted(table["rows"], key=query.sort_key):
446	                version = self._visible(table["rows"][pk], None, self._horizon)
447	                if version is not None:
448	                    rows.append([pk, version["values"]])
449	            tables[name] = {
450	                "columns": table["columns"],
451	                "primary_key": table["primary_key"],
452	                "indexes": sorted(table["indexes"]),
453	                "rows": rows,
454	            }
455	        return {"format": DB_FORMAT, "tables": tables}
456	
457	    def _committed_entries(self, table, column):
458	        """Sorted ``(value, pk)`` index entries of the committed row state."""
459	        entries = []
460	        for pk, versions in table["rows"].items():
461	            version = self._visible(versions, None, self._horizon)
462	            if version is None:
463	                continue
464	            value = version["values"].get(column)
465	            if value is not None:
466	                entries.append((value, pk))
467	        entries.sort(key=btree.entry_key)
468	        return entries

470	    def _check_index_pages(self, refs):
471	        """Validate the state blob's index page references against the rows.
472	
473	        Every referenced B+ tree is walked and checked structurally (page ids,
474	        checksums via the pager, root to leaf connectivity, key order) and its
475	        entries must reproduce exactly the committed index entries of its
476	        column; every catalog index must be referenced exactly once.  Any
477	        mismatch means the image cannot be trusted, so it raises
478	        :class:`StorageError`.
479	        """
480	        if not isinstance(refs, list):
481	            raise StorageError("state record holds malformed index references")
482	        seen = set()
483	        for ref in refs:
484	            if (
485	                not isinstance(ref, dict)
486	                or not {"table", "column", "root"} <= set(ref)
487	                or not isinstance(ref["table"], str)
488	                or not isinstance(ref["column"], str)
489	            ):
490	                raise StorageError("state record holds a malformed index reference")
491	            name, column = ref["table"], ref["column"]
492	            if (name, column) in seen:
493	                raise StorageError("duplicate index pages for %s.%s" % (name, column))
494	            seen.add((name, column))
495	            table = self.tables.get(name)
496	            if table is None or column not in table["indexes"]:
497	                raise StorageError("index pages reference unknown index %s.%s" % (name, column))
498	            entries = btree.read_entries(
499	                self.pager.read_page, ref["root"], name, column, self.pager.page_count()
500	            )
501	            count = ref.get("entries")
502	            if count is not None and (
503	                not isinstance(count, int) or isinstance(count, bool) or count != len(entries)
504	            ):
505	                raise StorageError(
506	                    "index pages for %s.%s hold %d entries, state record says %r"
507	                    % (name, column, len(entries), count)
508	                )
509	            want = [list(e) for e in self._committed_entries(table, column)]
510	            if [list(e) for e in entries] != want:
511	                raise StorageError(
512	                    "index pages for %s.%s do not match the committed rows" % (name, column)
513	                )
514	        for name, table in self.tables.items():
515	            for column in table["indexes"]:
516	                if (name, column) not in seen:
517	                    raise StorageError(
518	                        "index %s.%s has no pages in the state record" % (name, column)
519	                    )
520	
521	    def _index_layout(self, first_page):
522	        """Serialize every index's committed entries into B+ tree pages.
523	
524	        Returns ``(refs, layout)``: the index references recorded in the
525	        state blob and a list of ``(first_page, payloads)`` page extents.
526	        """
527	        refs = []
528	        layout = []
529	        for name in sorted(self.tables):
530	            table = self.tables[name]
531	            for column in sorted(table["indexes"]):
532	                entries = self._committed_entries(table, column)
533	                payloads, root, height = btree.build_pages(
534	                    name, column, entries, first_page, self.pager.payload_size
535	                )
536	                refs.append({
537	                    "table": name,
538	                    "column": column,
539	                    "root": root,
540	                    "entries": len(entries),
541	                    "height": height,
542	                })
543	                layout.append((first_page, payloads))
544	                first_page += len(payloads)
545	        return refs, layout
546	
547	    def _persist(self, tx):
548	        """Write audit, state and index pages plus the meta page, then commit.
549	
550	        The index references live in the state blob (which spans as many
551	        pages as it needs), so the single meta page keeps its baseline shape
552	        and size no matter how many indexes exist.  The references name root
553	        page ids, which depend on the state blob's own length, so the layout
554	        is iterated to a fixed point before anything is written.
555	        """
556	        audit_lsn = self.pager.peek_lsn()
557	        entry = {"lsn": audit_lsn, "txid": tx.txid, "at": self._now(), "ops": list(tx.ops)}
558	        audit = self._audit + [entry]
559	        audit_blob = json.dumps(audit, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
560	        audit_pages = self._write_chunks(tx.txid, AUDIT_PAGE, audit_blob)
561	        state_first = AUDIT_PAGE + audit_pages
562	        state = self._snapshot()
563	        refs = []
564	        layout = []
565	        for _ in range(8):
566	            state["index_refs"] = refs
567	            state_blob = json.dumps(state, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
568	            state_pages = max(1, -(-len(state_blob) // self.pager.payload_size))
569	            new_refs, layout = self._index_layout(state_first + state_pages)
570	            if new_refs == refs:
571	                break
572	            refs = new_refs
573	        else:
574	            raise StorageError("index page layout did not converge")
575	        state_pages = self._write_chunks(tx.txid, state_first, state_blob)
576	        for first, payloads in layout:
577	            for offset, payload in enumerate(payloads):
578	                self.pager.write_page(tx.txid, first + offset, payload)
579	        meta_lsn = self.pager.peek_lsn()
580	        meta = {
581	            "format": STATE_FORMAT,
582	            "lsn": meta_lsn + 1,
583	            "txid": tx.txid,
584	            "audit_page": AUDIT_PAGE,
585	            "audit_pages": audit_pages,
586	            "audit_len": len(audit_blob),
587	            "state_page": state_first,
588	            "state_pages": state_pages,
589	            "state_len": len(state_blob),
590	            "next_txid": self._next_txid,
591	            "horizon": self._horizon,
592	        }
593	        self.pager.write_page(tx.txid, META_PAGE, json.dumps(meta, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8"))
594	        lsn = self.pager.commit(tx.txid)
595	        self._audit = audit
596	        self.lsn = lsn
597	        return lsn

599	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- definition
600	    def _check_definition(self, name, columns, primary_key, indexes):
601	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
602	            raise StorageError("table name must be a non-empty string")
603	        if not isinstance(columns, list) or not columns:
604	            raise StorageError("table %s needs at least one column" % name)
605	        seen = set()
606	        for column in columns:
607	            if not isinstance(column, dict):
608	                raise StorageError("column definitions must be objects")
609	            cname = column.get("name")
610	            if not isinstance(cname, str) or not cname.strip():
611	                raise StorageError("column name must be a non-empty string")
612	            if cname in seen:
613	                raise StorageError("duplicate column %s" % cname)
614	            seen.add(cname)
615	            if column.get("type") not in TYPES:
616	                raise StorageError("column %s has unsupported type %r" % (cname, column.get("type")))
617	            for flag in ("nullable", "unique"):
618	                if flag in column and not isinstance(column[flag], bool):
619	                    raise StorageError("column %s: %s must be a boolean" % (cname, flag))
620	            if "references" in column:
621	                self._check_reference(name, column, column["references"])
622	        if primary_key not in seen:
623	            raise StorageError("primary key %r is not a column of table %s" % (primary_key, name))
624	        if indexes is None:
625	            indexes = []
626	        if not isinstance(indexes, (list, tuple)):
627	            raise StorageError("indexes must be a list of column names")
628	        for column in indexes:
629	            if column not in seen:
630	                raise StorageError("index column %r is not a column of table %s" % (column, name))

632	    def _check_reference(self, table, column, ref):
633	        """Validate one ``references`` object against the existing catalog."""
634	        cname = column["name"]
635	        if not isinstance(ref, dict) or set(ref) != {"table", "column"}:
636	            raise StorageError(
637	                "column %s of table %s: references must be an object "
638	                "with exactly 'table' and 'column'" % (cname, table)
639	            )
640	        target_name = ref["table"]
641	        target_column = ref["column"]
642	        if not isinstance(target_name, str) or not target_name.strip():
643	            raise StorageError("column %s of table %s: references.table must be a non-empty string" % (cname, table))
644	        if not isinstance(target_column, str) or not target_column.strip():
645	            raise StorageError("column %s of table %s: references.column must be a non-empty string" % (cname, table))
646	        target = self.tables.get(target_name)
647	        if target is None:
648	            raise StorageError(
649	                "column %s of table %s references unknown table %s" % (cname, table, target_name)
650	            )
651	        if target_column != target["primary_key"]:
652	            raise StorageError(
653	                "column %s of table %s references %s.%s, which is not the primary key"
654	                % (cname, table, target_name, target_column)
655	            )
656	        pk_column = [c for c in target["columns"] if c["name"] == target["primary_key"]][0]
657	        if pk_column["type"] != column["type"]:
658	            raise StorageError(
659	                "column %s of table %s has type %s but references %s.%s of type %s"
660	                % (cname, table, column["type"], target_name, target_column, pk_column["type"])
661	            )

663	    def create_table(self, name, columns, primary_key, indexes=None):
664	        with self._lock:
665	            self._check_definition(name, columns, primary_key, indexes)
666	            if name in self.tables:
667	                raise StorageError("table %s already exists" % name)
668	            tx = self._begin()
669	            try:
670	                catalog = []
671	                for column in columns:
672	                    entry = {
673	                        "name": column["name"],
674	                        "type": column["type"],
675	                        "nullable": False if column["name"] == primary_key else bool(column.get("nullable", True)),
676	                        "unique": True if column["name"] == primary_key else bool(column.get("unique", False)),
677	                    }
678	                    if column.get("references") is not None:
679	                        entry["references"] = {
680	                            "table": column["references"]["table"],
681	                            "column": column["references"]["column"],
682	                        }
683	                    catalog.append(entry)
684	                self.tables[name] = {
685	                    "name": name,
686	                    "columns": catalog,
687	                    "primary_key": primary_key,
688	                    "indexes": {},
689	                    "rows": {},
690	                }
691	                tx._undo.append(lambda: self._drop_table(name))
692	                for column in (indexes or []):
693	                    self._create_index(tx, name, column)
694	                tx.ops.append({
695	                    "op": "create_table",
696	                    "table": name,
697	                    "primary_key": primary_key,
698	                    "indexes": sorted(indexes or []),
699	                })
700	                tx.commit()
701	            except Exception:
702	                tx.rollback()
703	                raise
704	            return self.table_info(name)

706	    def _drop_table(self, name):
707	        self.tables.pop(name, None)
708	        for key in [k for k in self._indexes if k[0] == name]:
709	            self._indexes.pop(key, None)
710	
711	    def create_index(self, table, column):
712	        with self._lock:
713	            tx = self._begin()
714	            try:
715	                name = self._create_index(tx, table, column)
716	                tx.ops.append({"op": "create_index", "table": table, "column": column})
717	                tx.commit()
718	            except Exception:
719	                tx.rollback()
720	                raise
721	            return name

723	    def _create_index(self, tx, table, column):
724	        table_obj = self._table(table)
725	        if column not in {col["name"] for col in table_obj["columns"]}:
726	            raise StorageError("unknown column %s.%s" % (table, column))
727	        if column in table_obj["indexes"]:
728	            raise StorageError("index on %s.%s already exists" % (table, column))
729	        table_obj["indexes"][column] = "%s_%s_idx" % (table, column)
730	        self._indexes[(table, column)] = btree.BPlusTree()
731	        self._rebuild_indexes(table_obj)
732	        tx._undo.append(lambda: self._drop_index(table, column))
733	        return table_obj["indexes"][column]
734	
735	    def _drop_index(self, table, column):
736	        self._indexes.pop((table, column), None)
737	        table_obj = self.tables.get(table)
738	        if table_obj is not None:
739	            table_obj["indexes"].pop(column, None)
740	
741	    def _rebuild_indexes(self, table):
742	        for column in table["indexes"]:
743	            tree = self._indexes.setdefault((table["name"], column), btree.BPlusTree())
744	            tree.bulk_load(self._committed_entries(table, column))

746	    def _index_add(self, table, values):
747	        """Add index entries for one row version; never duplicates.
748	
749	        Entries of superseded versions are kept until nothing can read them
750	        any more (see ``_finish``), so an index scan stays correct for readers
751	        that still hold an older snapshot.
752	        """
753	        table_obj = self.tables[table]
754	        pk = values[table_obj["primary_key"]]
755	        for column in table_obj["indexes"]:
756	            value = values.get(column)
757	            if value is None:
758	                continue
759	            tree = self._indexes.setdefault((table, column), btree.BPlusTree())
760	            tree.insert((value, pk))

762	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- row writes
763	    def _build_values(self, table, row, current):
764	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
765	            raise ConstraintError("row must be a JSON object")
766	        columns = {col["name"]: col for col in table["columns"]}
767	        unknown = sorted(key for key in row if key not in columns)
768	        if unknown:
769	            raise StorageError("unknown column(s) %s on table %s" % (", ".join(unknown), table["name"]))
770	        merged = dict(current or {})
771	        merged.update(row)
772	        values = {}
773	        for column in table["columns"]:
774	            name = column["name"]
775	            value = merged.get(name)
776	            if value is None:
777	                if not column["nullable"]:
778	                    raise ConstraintError("column %s of %s may not be null" % (name, table["name"]))
779	                values[name] = None
780	            elif not query.check_type(value, column["type"]):
781	                raise ConstraintError(
782	                    "column %s of %s expects %s" % (name, table["name"], column["type"])
783	                )
784	            else:
785	                values[name] = value
786	        return values

788	    def _check_unique(self, tx, table, values, exclude_pk):
789	        primary_key = table["primary_key"]
790	        for column in table["columns"]:
791	            name = column["name"]
792	            if name == primary_key or not column["unique"]:
793	                continue
794	            value = values[name]
795	            if value is None:
796	                continue
797	            for pk, versions in table["rows"].items():
798	                if pk == exclude_pk:
799	                    continue
800	                version = self._visible(versions, tx.txid, tx.snapshot)
801	                if version is not None and version["values"].get(name) == value:
802	                    raise ConstraintError("unique constraint violated on %s.%s" % (table["name"], name))
803	                seen = self._conflicting_writes(versions, tx)
804	                if seen is not None and seen["values"].get(name) == value and seen["deleted"] is None:
805	                    raise ConflictError(
806	                        "concurrent write on unique column %s.%s" % (table["name"], name)
807	                    )

809	    # ---------------------------------------------------------- foreign keys
810	    def _fk_visible(self, versions, txid, horizon):
811	        """Visibility for foreign key checks.
812	
813	        Unlike :meth:`_visible` (which keeps a version readable to the
814	        transaction that deleted it, so an update chain stays readable), a
815	        row this transaction deleted no longer counts here: it will not be
816	        part of the committed state, so it can neither satisfy a child
817	        reference nor keep a parent alive.
818	        """
819	        best = None
820	        for version in versions:
821	            created = version["created"]
822	            deleted = version["deleted"]
823	            if created != txid and not (self._is_committed(created) and created <= horizon):
824	                continue
825	            if deleted is None:
826	                best = version
827	            elif deleted != txid and not (self._is_committed(deleted) and deleted <= horizon):
828	                best = version
829	        return best
830	
831	    def _referrers(self, table_name):
832	        """``(child_table, column)`` pairs whose foreign key targets ``table_name``."""
833	        found = []
834	        for child_name, child in self.tables.items():
835	            for column in child["columns"]:
836	                ref = column.get("references")
837	                if ref is not None and ref["table"] == table_name:
838	                    found.append((child_name, column["name"]))
839	        return found
840	
841	    def _check_fk_values(self, tx, table, values):
842	        """Every non-null foreign key value must resolve in this transaction's view."""
843	        for column in table["columns"]:
844	            ref = column.get("references")
845	            if ref is None:
846	                continue
847	            value = values.get(column["name"])
848	            if value is None:
849	                continue
850	            parent = self.tables[ref["table"]]
851	            versions = parent["rows"].get(value)
852	            version = self._fk_visible(versions, tx.txid, tx.snapshot) if versions else None
853	            if version is None:
854	                raise ConstraintError(
855	                    "foreign key violation on %s.%s: no row %r in table %s"
856	                    % (table["name"], column["name"], value, ref["table"])
857	                )

859	    def _check_fk_delete(self, tx, table_name, pk):
860	        """A parent row cannot be deleted while a visible child references it."""
861	        for child_name, column_name in self._referrers(table_name):
862	            child = self.tables[child_name]
863	            for versions in child["rows"].values():
864	                version = self._fk_visible(versions, tx.txid, tx.snapshot)
865	                if version is not None and version["values"].get(column_name) == pk:
866	                    raise ConstraintError(
867	                        "foreign key violation: row %r of table %s is still "
868	                        "referenced by %s.%s" % (pk, table_name, child_name, column_name)
869	                    )

871	    def _record_fk_refs(self, tx, table, values):
872	        for column in table["columns"]:
873	            ref = column.get("references")
874	            if ref is not None:
875	                value = values.get(column["name"])
876	                if value is not None:
877	                    tx._fk_refs.append((ref["table"], value))

879	    def _check_foreign_keys(self, tx):
880	        """Re-validate a committing transaction's foreign key effects.
881	
882	        A concurrent transaction may have committed after the per-operation
883	        checks ran — deleting a parent this transaction referenced, or
884	        inserting a child that references a parent it deleted.  Replaying the
885	        checks against the newest committed state (plus this transaction's
886	        own writes) keeps a commit from leaving a dangling reference behind.
887	        """
888	        for parent_name, pk in tx._fk_refs:
889	            parent = self.tables.get(parent_name)
890	            versions = parent["rows"].get(pk) if parent is not None else None
891	            version = self._fk_visible(versions, tx.txid, self._horizon) if versions else None
892	            if version is None:
893	                raise ConstraintError(
894	                    "foreign key violation: no row %r in table %s at commit" % (pk, parent_name)
895	                )
896	        for parent_name, pk in tx._fk_dels:
897	            for child_name, column_name in self._referrers(parent_name):
898	                child = self.tables[child_name]
899	                for versions in child["rows"].values():
900	                    version = self._fk_visible(versions, tx.txid, self._horizon)
901	                    if version is not None and version["values"].get(column_name) == pk:
902	                        raise ConstraintError(
903	                            "foreign key violation: row %r of table %s is still "
904	                            "referenced by %s.%s" % (pk, parent_name, child_name, column_name)
905	                        )

907	    def _insert(self, tx, table, row):
908	        table_obj = self._table(table)
909	        values = self._build_values(table_obj, row, None)
910	        pk = values[table_obj["primary_key"]]
911	        versions = table_obj["rows"].get(pk, [])
912	        if self._visible(versions, tx.txid, tx.snapshot) is not None:
913	            raise ConstraintError("duplicate primary key %r in table %s" % (pk, table))
914	        if self._conflicting_writes(versions, tx) is not None:
915	            raise ConflictError("primary key %r in table %s is written by another transaction" % (pk, table))
916	        self._check_unique(tx, table_obj, values, None)
917	        self._check_fk_values(tx, table_obj, values)
918	        version = {"created": tx.txid, "deleted": None, "values": values}
919	        table_obj["rows"].setdefault(pk, []).append(version)
920	        self._index_add(table, values)
921	
922	        def undo():
923	            chain = table_obj["rows"].get(pk)
924	            if chain and version in chain:
925	                chain.remove(version)
926	            if chain is not None and not chain:
927	                table_obj["rows"].pop(pk, None)
928	
929	        tx._undo.append(undo)
930	        self._record_fk_refs(tx, table_obj, values)
931	        tx.ops.append({"op": "insert", "table": table, "pk": pk, "row": values})
932	        return dict(values)

934	    def _update(self, tx, table, pk, patch):
935	        table_obj = self._table(table)
936	        pk = self._coerce_pk(table_obj, pk)
937	        if not isinstance(patch, dict) or not patch:
938	            raise StorageError("update needs a non-empty patch object")
939	        versions = table_obj["rows"].get(pk)
940	        version = self._visible(versions, tx.txid, tx.snapshot) if versions else None
941	        if version is None:
942	            if versions and self._conflicting_writes(versions, tx) is not None:
943	                raise ConflictError("row %r of %s was written after transaction %d started" % (pk, table, tx.txid))
944	            raise StorageError("row %r not found in table %s" % (pk, table))
945	        if self._conflicting_writes(versions, tx) is not None:
946	            raise ConflictError("row %r of %s was written after transaction %d started" % (pk, table, tx.txid))
947	        values = self._build_values(table_obj, patch, version["values"])
948	        if values[table_obj["primary_key"]] != pk:
949	            raise ConstraintError("primary key of %s may not be updated" % table)
950	        self._check_unique(tx, table_obj, values, pk)
951	        self._check_fk_values(tx, table_obj, values)
952	        version["deleted"] = tx.txid
953	        new_version = {"created": tx.txid, "deleted": None, "values": values}
954	        versions.append(new_version)
955	        self._index_add(table, values)
956	
957	        def undo():
958	            version["deleted"] = None
959	            if new_version in versions:
960	                versions.remove(new_version)
961	
962	        tx._undo.append(undo)
963	        self._record_fk_refs(tx, table_obj, values)
964	        tx.ops.append({"op": "update", "table": table, "pk": pk, "patch": dict(patch)})
965	        return dict(values)

967	    def _delete(self, tx, table, pk):
968	        table_obj = self._table(table)
969	        pk = self._coerce_pk(table_obj, pk)
970	        versions = table_obj["rows"].get(pk)
971	        version = self._visible(versions, tx.txid, tx.snapshot) if versions else None
972	        if version is None:
973	            if versions and self._conflicting_writes(versions, tx) is not None:
974	                raise ConflictError("row %r of %s was written after transaction %d started" % (pk, table, tx.txid))
975	            raise StorageError("row %r not found in table %s" % (pk, table))

1409	    def rollback_to(self, name):

1414	        protected even when the writes around them are undone.
1415	        """
1416	        self._check_active()
1417	        with self.engine._lock:
1418	            index = self._find_savepoint(name)
1419	            target = self._savepoints[index]
1420	            while len(self._undo) > target["undo"]:
1421	                self._undo.pop()()
1422	            del self.ops[target["ops"]:]
1423	            del self._fk_refs[target["fk_refs"]:]
1424	            del self._fk_dels[target["fk_dels"]:]

1448	    def commit(self):

1454	            if self.isolation == "serializable":
1455	                try:
1456	                    engine._check_read_conflicts(self)
1457	                except ConflictError:

1459	                    # good: undo row and index changes, write no audit record
1460	                    # and leave the committed lsn untouched.
1461	                    self._rollback_locked()
1462	                    engine.pager.abort(self.txid)
1463	                    self.state = "rolled_back"
1464	                    engine._finish(self, False)
1465	                    raise
1466	            try:
1467	                engine._check_foreign_keys(self)
1468	            except ConstraintError:

1472	                self._rollback_locked()
1473	                engine.pager.abort(self.txid)
1474	                self.state = "rolled_back"
1475	                engine._finish(self, False)
1476	                raise

1479	                engine._horizon = self.txid
1480	            try:

1482	            except Exception:

1484	                self._rollback_locked()
1485	                self.state = "failed"
1486	                raise
1487	            self.state = "committed"
1488	            self._undo = []
1489	            self._fk_refs = []
1490	            self._fk_dels = []
1491	            self._savepoints = []

1500	                self.engine.pager.abort(self.txid)
1501	            self.state = "rolled_back"
1502	            self.engine._finish(self, False)

1507	            self._undo.pop()()

1509	        self._fk_refs = []
1510	        self._fk_dels = []
1511	        self._savepoints = []

1	"""Standard library HTTP front end: JSON over HTTP/1.1.
2	
3	Routes
4	------
5	GET  /healthz                      -> {"ok": true}
6	POST /v1/tables                    -> 201 catalog info
7	GET  /v1/tables                    -> 200 {"tables": [...]}
8	POST /v1/tables/{table}/rows       -> 201 {"inserted": n}
9	GET  /v1/tables/{table}/rows/{pk}  -> 200 row / 404
10	POST /v1/query                     -> 200 {"rows": [...], "access": "index"|"scan"}
11	POST /v1/tx                        -> 200 {"committed": true, "lsn": n} / 409
12	GET  /v1/verify                    -> 200 integrity report
13	GET  /v1/audit?limit=n             -> 200 {"entries": [...], "count": n}
14	
15	Every failure is answered with a JSON body ``{"error": "..."}``.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import json
21	import re
22	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
23	from urllib.parse import parse_qs, unquote, urlparse
24	
25	from .engine import ConflictError, ConstraintError, Engine, StorageError
26	
27	ROW_PATH = re.compile(r"^/v1/tables/([^/]+)/rows(?:/(.*))?$")
28	
29	
30	def coerce(text, type_name):
31	    """Convert a path/text value into the declared column type."""
32	    if type_name == "int":
33	        try:
34	            return int(text)
35	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
36	            raise StorageError("value %r is not an int" % (text,))
37	    if type_name == "bool":
38	        lowered = str(text).lower()
39	        if lowered in ("true", "1"):
40	            return True
41	        if lowered in ("false", "0"):
42	            return False
43	        raise StorageError("value %r is not a bool" % (text,))
44	    return text
45	
46	
47	class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
48	    server_version = "kvse/0.1"
49	    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
50	
51	    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):  # keep CLI stdout clean
52	        return
53	
54	    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- plumbing
55	    def _send(self, status, payload):
56	        body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
57	        self.send_response(status)
58	        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
59	        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
60	        self.end_headers()
61	        self.wfile.write(body)
62	
63	    def _error(self, status, message):
64	        self._send(status, {"error": message})
65	
66	    def _status_for(self, exc):
67	        if isinstance(exc, (ConflictError, ConstraintError)):
68	            return 409
69	        return 400
70	
71	    def _body(self):
72	        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
73	        if length <= 0:
74	            return {}
75	        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
76	        try:
77	            data = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
78	        except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as exc:
79	            raise StorageError("invalid JSON body: %s" % exc)
80	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
81	            raise StorageError("request body must be a JSON object")
82	        return data
83	
84	    @property
85	    def engine(self):
86	        return self.server.engine
87	
88	    # -------------------------------------------------------------------- GET
89	    def do_GET(self):
90	        try:
91	            parsed = urlparse(self.path)
92	            path = parsed.path.rstrip("/") or "/"
93	            if path == "/healthz":
94	                return self._send(200, {"ok": True})
95	            if path == "/v1/tables":
96	                return self._send(200, {"tables": self.engine.list_tables()})
97	            if path == "/v1/verify":
98	                return self._send(200, self.engine.verify())
99	            if path == "/v1/audit":
100	                limit = parse_qs(parsed.query).get("limit", [None])[0]
101	                limit = int(limit) if limit not in (None, "") else None
102	                entries = self.engine.audit(limit=limit)
103	                return self._send(200, {"entries": entries, "count": len(entries)})
104	            match = ROW_PATH.match(path)
105	            if match:
106	                return self._get_row(unquote(match.group(1)), unquote(match.group(2) or ""))
107	            return self._error(404, "no route for GET %s" % path)
108	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - reported as a JSON error
109	            return self._error(self._status_for(exc), str(exc))
110	
111	    def _get_row(self, table, pk_text):
112	        if not self.engine.has_table(table):
113	            return self._error(404, "unknown table %s" % table)
114	        info = self.engine.table_info(table)
115	        column = [c for c in info["columns"] if c["name"] == info["primary_key"]][0]
116	        row = self.engine.get(table, coerce(pk_text, column["type"]))
117	        if row is None:
118	            return self._error(404, "row %s not found in table %s" % (pk_text, table))
119	        return self._send(200, row)
120	
121	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- POST
122	    def do_POST(self):
123	        try:
124	            path = urlparse(self.path).path.rstrip("/") or "/"
125	            if path == "/v1/tables":
126	                return self._create_table(self._body())
127	            if path == "/v1/query":
128	                return self._query(self._body())
129	            if path == "/v1/tx":
130	                return self._tx(self._body())
131	            match = ROW_PATH.match(path)
132	            if match and not match.group(2):
133	                return self._insert_rows(unquote(match.group(1)), self._body())
134	            return self._error(404, "no route for POST %s" % path)
135	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - reported as a JSON error
136	            return self._error(self._status_for(exc), str(exc))
137	
138	    def _create_table(self, body):
139	        name = body.get("name")
140	        info = self.engine.create_table(
141	            name, body.get("columns") or [], body.get("primary_key"), body.get("indexes") or []
142	        )
143	        return self._send(201, dict(info, index_names=sorted(info["indexes"])))
144	
145	    def _insert_rows(self, table, body):
146	        if not self.engine.has_table(table):
147	            return self._error(404, "unknown table %s" % table)
148	        rows = body.get("rows")
149	        if not isinstance(rows, list) or not rows:
150	            raise StorageError("body must contain a non-empty 'rows' array")
151	        tx = self.engine.begin()
152	        try:
153	            for row in rows:
154	                tx.insert(table, row)
155	            lsn = tx.commit()
156	        except Exception:
157	            tx.rollback()
158	            raise
159	        return self._send(201, {"inserted": len(rows), "table": table, "lsn": lsn})
160	
161	    def _query(self, body):
162	        table = body.get("table")
163	        if not self.engine.has_table(table):
164	            return self._error(404, "unknown table %s" % table)
165	        result = self.engine.query(
166	            table,
167	            columns=body.get("columns"),
168	            where=body.get("where"),
169	            index_hint=body.get("index_hint"),
170	            limit=body.get("limit"),
171	            order_by=body.get("order_by"),
172	        )
173	        return self._send(200, result)
174	
175	    def _tx(self, body):
176	        ops = body.get("ops")
177	        if not isinstance(ops, list) or not ops:
178	            raise StorageError("body must contain a non-empty 'ops' array")
179	        result = self.engine.transaction(
180	            ops, snapshot=body.get("snapshot_txid"), isolation=body.get("isolation")
181	        )
182	        return self._send(200, result)
183	
184	
185	class Server(ThreadingHTTPServer):
186	    daemon_threads = True
187	    allow_reuse_address = True
188	
189	    def __init__(self, address, engine):
190	        self.engine = engine
191	        super().__init__(address, Handler)
192	
193	
194	def create_server(engine, host="127.0.0.1", port=8080):
195	    """Bind a threading HTTP server for ``engine`` and return it unstarted."""
196	    if not isinstance(engine, Engine):
197	        raise StorageError("create_server expects an Engine instance")
198	    return Server((host, int(port)), engine)
199

1	"""Tiny query subset: scan, point get and index range on one column.
2	
3	The module also owns the two small helpers shared with the engine
4	(``check_type`` for column types and ``sort_key`` for deterministic row
5	ordering) so that no import cycle is needed.
6	
7	Supported predicates are ``[(column, op, value)]`` with ``op`` taken from
8	``OPS``.  The access path is chosen by the first predicate: when it targets an
9	indexed column and the operator can be served by a range scan, the index is
10	used, otherwise the table is scanned.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	from .pager import StorageError
16	
17	OPS = ("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
18	INDEX_OPS = ("=", "<", "<=", ">", ">=")
19	
20	
21	def check_type(value, type_name):
22	    """True when ``value`` is a legal value for a column of ``type_name``."""
23	    if type_name == "int":
24	        return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
25	    if type_name == "bool":
26	        return isinstance(value, bool)
27	    if type_name == "text":
28	        return isinstance(value, str)
29	    return False
30	
31	
32	def sort_key(value):
33	    """Ordering key that keeps mixed int/str/bool values deterministic."""
34	    if isinstance(value, bool):
35	        return (0, int(value), "")
36	    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
37	        return (1, value, "")
38	    return (2, 0, "" if value is None else str(value))
39	
40	
41	def compare(op, left, right):
42	    if op == "=":
43	        return left == right
44	    if op == "!=":
45	        return left != right
46	    if left is None or right is None:
47	        return False
48	    try:
49	        if op == "<":
50	            return left < right
51	        if op == "<=":
52	            return left <= right
53	        if op == ">":
54	            return left > right
55	        if op == ">=":
56	            return left >= right
57	    except TypeError:
58	        raise StorageError("cannot compare %r with %r" % (left, right))
59	    raise StorageError("unsupported operator %r" % (op,))
60	
61	
62	def normalize_where(source, table, where):
63	    """Validate ``where`` and return a list of ``(column, op, value)``."""
64	    info = source.table_info(table)
65	    columns = {col["name"]: col for col in info["columns"]}
66	    if where is None:
67	        return []
68	    if not isinstance(where, (list, tuple)):
69	        raise StorageError("where must be a list of [column, op, value]")
70	    conds = []
71	    for item in where:
72	        if isinstance(item, (list, tuple)) and len(item) == 3:
73	            column, op, value = item
74	        elif isinstance(item, dict):
75	            column = item.get("column", item.get("col"))
76	            op = item.get("op", "=")
77	            value = item.get("value")
78	        else:
79	            raise StorageError("each where predicate must be [column, op, value]")
80	        if op not in OPS:
81	            raise StorageError("unsupported operator %r" % (op,))
82	        if column not in columns:
83	            raise StorageError("unknown column %s.%s" % (table, column))
84	        if value is not None and not check_type(value, columns[column]["type"]):
85	            raise StorageError(
86	                "predicate on %s.%s expects %s" % (table, column, columns[column]["type"])
87	            )
88	        conds.append((column, op, value))
89	    return conds
90	
91	
92	def _choose(info, conds, index_hint):
93	    indexes = info["indexes"]
94	    if index_hint and index_hint != "scan":
95	        column = index_hint if index_hint in indexes else None
96	        if column is None:
97	            for name, index_name in indexes.items():
98	                if index_name == index_hint:
99	                    column = name
100	                    break
101	        if column is None:
102	            raise StorageError("no usable index named %s on table %s" % (index_hint, info["name"]))
103	        for cond in conds:
104	            if cond[0] == column and cond[1] in INDEX_OPS:
105	                return "index", indexes[column]
106	        return "scan", None
107	    if conds and conds[0][1] in INDEX_OPS and conds[0][0] in indexes:
108	        return "index", indexes[conds[0][0]]
109	    return "scan", None
110	
111	
112	def plan(source, table, columns=None, where=None, index_hint=None, limit=None, order_by=None):
113	    conds = normalize_where(source, table, where)
114	    info = source.table_info(table)
115	    access, index_name = _choose(info, conds, index_hint)
116	    return {
117	        "table": table,
118	        "access": access,
119	        "index": index_name,
120	        "columns": list(columns) if columns else None,
121	        "where": [list(c) for c in conds],
122	        "limit": limit,
123	        "order_by": order_by,
124	    }
125	
126	
127	def explain(source, table, where=None, index_hint=None, **kwargs):
128	    chosen = plan(source, table, where=where, index_hint=index_hint, **kwargs)
129	    return {"access": chosen["access"], "index": chosen["index"]}
130	
131	
132	def execute(source, table, columns=None, where=None, index_hint=None, limit=None, order_by=None):
133	    conds = normalize_where(source, table, where)
134	    info = source.table_info(table)
135	    access, index_name = _choose(info, conds, index_hint)
136	    if access == "index":
137	        column, op, value = conds[0]
138	        if op == "=":
139	            rows = source.index_get(table, column, value)
140	        elif op in ("<", "<="):
141	            rows = source.index_range(table, column, None, value)
142	        else:
143	            rows = source.index_range(table, column, value, None)
144	        key_column = order_by or column
145	    else:
146	        rows = source.scan(table)
147	        key_column = order_by or info["primary_key"]
148	    if conds:
149	        rows = [row for row in rows if all(compare(op, row.get(col), val) for col, op, val in conds)]
150	    if order_by and order_by not in {col["name"] for col in info["columns"]}:
151	        raise StorageError("unknown column %s.%s" % (table, order_by))
152	    rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda row: sort_key(row.get(key_column)))
153	    if limit is not None:
154	        limit = int(limit)
155	        if limit < 0:
156	            raise StorageError("limit must be greater than or equal to 0")
157	        rows = rows[:limit]
158	    if columns:
159	        known = {col["name"] for col in info["columns"]}
160	        unknown = sorted(col for col in columns if col not in known)
161	        if unknown:
162	            raise StorageError("unknown column(s) %s on table %s" % (", ".join(unknown), table))
163	        rows = [{col: row.get(col) for col in columns} for row in rows]
164	    return {"rows": rows, "access": access, "index": index_name, "table": table}
165	
166	
167	def select(source, table, columns=None, where=None, index_hint=None, limit=None, order_by=None):
168	    """Convenience wrapper returning just the projected rows."""
169	    return execute(
170	        source,
171	        table,
172	        columns=columns,
173	        where=where,
174	        index_hint=index_hint,
175	        limit=limit,
176	        order_by=order_by,
177	    )["rows"]

1	"""Command line interface.
2	
3	Usage
4	-----
5	python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] serve [--host H] [--port P]
6	python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] create-table --file table.json
7	python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] insert --table T --file rows.json
8	python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] get --table T --pk K
9	python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] query --table T --where 'col>=value'
10	python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] verify
11	python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] tx-demo
12	
13	Every command prints a single line of JSON on stdout and exits 0; any failure
14	prints a single line ``{"error": ...}`` on stderr and exits 1.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import argparse
20	import json
21	import sys
22	
23	from .engine import ConflictError, Engine
24	from .http_app import create_server
25	from .pager import StorageError
26	
27	OPS_BY_LENGTH = ("!=", "<=", ">=", "=", "<", ">")
28	
29	
30	def emit(payload, stream=None):
31	    stream = stream if stream is not None else sys.stdout
32	    stream.write(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
33	    stream.flush()
34	
35	
36	def load_json(path):
37	    try:
38	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
39	            return json.load(fh)
40	    except OSError as exc:
41	        raise StorageError("cannot read %s: %s" % (path, exc))
42	    except ValueError as exc:
43	        raise StorageError("%s does not contain valid JSON: %s" % (path, exc))
44	
45	
46	def literal(text):
47	    if text.lower() == "true":
48	        return True
49	    if text.lower() == "false":
50	        return False
51	    try:
52	        return int(text)
53	    except ValueError:
54	        pass
55	    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == text[-1] and text[0] in ("'", '"'):
56	        return text[1:-1]
57	    return text
58	
59	
60	def parse_where(text):
61	    for op in OPS_BY_LENGTH:
62	        index = text.find(op)
63	        if index > 0:
64	            return [(text[:index].strip(), op, literal(text[index + len(op):].strip()))]
65	    raise StorageError("--where must look like <column><op><value>")
66	
67	
68	def rows_from(data):
69	    if isinstance(data, list):
70	        return data
71	    if isinstance(data, dict) and isinstance(data.get("rows"), list):
72	        return data["rows"]
73	    if isinstance(data, dict):
74	        return [data]
75	    raise StorageError("--file must hold a row object or an array of rows")
76	
77	
78	def build_parser():
79	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="kvse", description="embedded relational storage engine")
80	    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default="./kvse_data", help="directory with data.pages and wal.log")
81	    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
82	
83	    serve = commands.add_parser("serve", help="run the HTTP API")
84	    serve.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
85	    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8080)
86	
87	    create = commands.add_parser("create-table", help="create a table from a JSON file")
88	    create.add_argument("--file", required=True)
89	
90	    insert = commands.add_parser("insert", help="insert rows from a JSON file")
91	    insert.add_argument("--table", required=True)
92	    insert.add_argument("--file", required=True)
93	
94	    get = commands.add_parser("get", help="point get by primary key")
95	    get.add_argument("--table", required=True)
96	    get.add_argument("--pk", required=True)
97	
98	    query = commands.add_parser("query", help="run the query subset")
99	    query.add_argument("--table", required=True)
100	    query.add_argument("--where", default=None)
101	    query.add_argument("--columns", default=None)
102	    query.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None)
103	    query.add_argument("--order-by", default=None)
104	
105	    commands.add_parser("verify", help="report pages, WAL records and checksums")
106	    commands.add_parser("tx-demo", help="demonstrate commit, rollback and a conflict")
107	    return parser
108	
109	
110	def cmd_serve(args):
111	    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
112	    server = create_server(engine, args.host, args.port)
113	    host, port = server.server_address[0], server.server_address[1]
114	    emit({"serving": True, "host": host, "port": port, "data_dir": engine.root})
115	    try:
116	        server.serve_forever()
117	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
118	        pass
119	    finally:
120	        server.server_close()
121	    return 0
122	
123	
124	def cmd_create_table(args):
125	    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
126	    data = load_json(args.file)
127	    info = engine.create_table(
128	        data.get("name"), data.get("columns") or [], data.get("primary_key"), data.get("indexes") or []
129	    )
130	    emit({"created": info["name"], "primary_key": info["primary_key"],
131	          "indexes": sorted(info["indexes"]), "columns": [c["name"] for c in info["columns"]]})
132	    return 0
133	
134	
135	def cmd_insert(args):
136	    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
137	    rows = rows_from(load_json(args.file))
138	    tx = engine.begin()
139	    try:
140	        for row in rows:
141	            tx.insert(args.table, row)
142	        lsn = tx.commit()
143	    except Exception:
144	        tx.rollback()
145	        raise
146	    emit({"inserted": len(rows), "table": args.table, "lsn": lsn})
147	    return 0
148	
149	
150	def cmd_get(args):
151	    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
152	    if not engine.has_table(args.table):
153	        raise StorageError("unknown table %s" % args.table)
154	    row = engine.get(args.table, args.pk)
155	    if row is None:
156	        raise StorageError("row %s not found in table %s" % (args.pk, args.table))
157	    emit(row)
158	    return 0

161	def cmd_query(args):
162	    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
163	    where = parse_where(args.where) if args.where else None
164	    columns = [c.strip() for c in args.columns.split(",")] if args.columns else None
165	    emit(engine.query(args.table, columns=columns, where=where, limit=args.limit, order_by=args.order_by))
166	    return 0
167	
168	
169	def cmd_verify(args):
170	    emit(Engine(args.data_dir).verify())
171	    return 0
172	
173	
174	def cmd_tx_demo(args):
175	    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
176	    if not engine.has_table("demo_items"):
177	        engine.create_table(
178	            "demo_items",
179	            [
180	                {"name": "id", "type": "int", "nullable": False},
181	                {"name": "label", "type": "text", "nullable": False, "unique": True},
182	                {"name": "qty", "type": "int"},
183	            ],
184	            "id",
185	            indexes=["label", "qty"],
186	        )

"""Command line interface.

Usage
-----
python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] serve [--host H] [--port P]
python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] create-table --file table.json
python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] insert --table T --file rows.json
python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] get --table T --pk K
python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] query --table T --where 'col>=value'
python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] verify
python3 -m kvse [--data-dir DIR] tx-demo

Every command prints a single line of JSON on stdout and exits 0; any failure
prints a single line ``{"error": ...}`` on stderr and exits 1.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys

from .engine import ConflictError, Engine
from .http_app import create_server
from .pager import StorageError

OPS_BY_LENGTH = ("!=", "<=", ">=", "=", "<", ">")


def emit(payload, stream=None):
    stream = stream if stream is not None else sys.stdout
    stream.write(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    stream.flush()


def load_json(path):
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return json.load(fh)
    except OSError as exc:
        raise StorageError("cannot read %s: %s" % (path, exc))
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise StorageError("%s does not contain valid JSON: %s" % (path, exc))


def literal(text):
    if text.lower() == "true":
        return True
    if text.lower() == "false":
        return False
    try:
        return int(text)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == text[-1] and text[0] in ("'", '"'):
        return text[1:-1]
    return text


def parse_where(text):
    for op in OPS_BY_LENGTH:
        index = text.find(op)
        if index > 0:
            return [(text[:index].strip(), op, literal(text[index + len(op):].strip()))]
    raise StorageError("--where must look like <column><op><value>")


def rows_from(data):
    if isinstance(data, list):
        return data
    if isinstance(data, dict) and isinstance(data.get("rows"), list):
        return data["rows"]
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        return [data]
    raise StorageError("--file must hold a row object or an array of rows")


def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="kvse", description="embedded relational storage engine")
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default="./kvse_data", help="directory with data.pages and wal.log")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    serve = commands.add_parser("serve", help="run the HTTP API")
    serve.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8080)

    create = commands.add_parser("create-table", help="create a table from a JSON file")
    create.add_argument("--file", required=True)

    insert = commands.add_parser("insert", help="insert rows from a JSON file")
    insert.add_argument("--table", required=True)
    insert.add_argument("--file", required=True)

    get = commands.add_parser("get", help="point get by primary key")
    get.add_argument("--table", required=True)
    get.add_argument("--pk", required=True)

    query = commands.add_parser("query", help="run the query subset")
    query.add_argument("--table", required=True)
    query.add_argument("--where", default=None)
    query.add_argument("--columns", default=None)
    query.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None)
    query.add_argument("--order-by", default=None)

    commands.add_parser("verify", help="report pages, WAL records and checksums")
    commands.add_parser("tx-demo", help="demonstrate commit, rollback and a conflict")
    return parser


def cmd_serve(args):
    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
    server = create_server(engine, args.host, args.port)
    host, port = server.server_address[0], server.server_address[1]
    emit({"serving": True, "host": host, "port": port, "data_dir": engine.root})
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()
    return 0


def cmd_create_table(args):
    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
    data = load_json(args.file)
    info = engine.create_table(
        data.get("name"), data.get("columns") or [], data.get("primary_key"), data.get("indexes") or []
    )
    emit({"created": info["name"], "primary_key": info["primary_key"],
          "indexes": sorted(info["indexes"]), "columns": [c["name"] for c in info["columns"]]})
    return 0


def cmd_insert(args):
    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
    rows = rows_from(load_json(args.file))
    tx = engine.begin()
    try:
        for row in rows:
            tx.insert(args.table, row)
        lsn = tx.commit()
    except Exception:
        tx.rollback()
        raise
    emit({"inserted": len(rows), "table": args.table, "lsn": lsn})
    return 0


def cmd_get(args):
    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
    if not engine.has_table(args.table):
        raise StorageError("unknown table %s" % args.table)
    row = engine.get(args.table, args.pk)
    if row is None:
        raise StorageError("row %s not found in table %s" % (args.pk, args.table))
    emit(row)
    return 0


def cmd_query(args):
    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
    where = parse_where(args.where) if args.where else None
    columns = [c.strip() for c in args.columns.split(",")] if args.columns else None
    emit(engine.query(args.table, columns=columns, where=where, limit=args.limit, order_by=args.order_by))
    return 0


def cmd_verify(args):
    emit(Engine(args.data_dir).verify())
    return 0


def cmd_tx_demo(args):
    engine = Engine(args.data_dir)
    if not engine.has_table("demo_items"):
        engine.create_table(
            "demo_items",
            [
                {"name": "id", "type": "int", "nullable": False},
                {"name": "label", "type": "text", "nullable": False, "unique": True},
                {"name": "qty", "type": "int"},
            ],
            "id",
            indexes=["label", "qty"],
        )
    report = {}
    tx = engine.begin()
    tx.insert("demo_items", {"id": 1, "label": "alpha", "qty": 5})
    report["commit_lsn"] = tx.commit()

    tx = engine.begin()
    tx.insert("demo_items", {"id": 2, "label": "beta", "qty": 9})
    report["rolled_back"] = tx.rollback()

    reader = engine.begin()
    writer = engine.begin()
    writer.update("demo_items", 1, {"qty": 42})
    report["second_commit_lsn"] = writer.commit()
    report["snapshot_still_sees"] = reader.get("demo_items", 1)
    try:
        reader.update("demo_items", 1, {"qty": 43})
        report["conflict"] = False
    except ConflictError as exc:
        report["conflict"] = True
        report["conflict_error"] = str(exc)
        reader.rollback()
    report["index_range_qty_0_100"] = [r["id"] for r in engine.index_range("demo_items", "qty", 0, 100)]
    report["access"] = engine.explain("demo_items", where=[("qty", ">=", 1)])
    report["audit_txids"] = [entry["txid"] for entry in engine.audit()]
    emit(report)
    return 0


COMMANDS = {
    "serve": cmd_serve,
    "create-table": cmd_create_table,
    "insert": cmd_insert,
    "get": cmd_get,
    "query": cmd_query,
    "verify": cmd_verify,
    "tx-demo": cmd_tx_demo,
}


def main(argv=None):
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return COMMANDS[args.command](args)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - single line JSON error on stderr
        emit({"error": str(exc)}, sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
